blocks.text: Many ask why the Jews, or the Pharisees, are repeatedly ^{a)} called γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν [gennēmata echidnōn], brood of vipers. Most think that this alludes to the tradition that the viper is born by gnawing through its mother's womb, because the Jews showed themselves ungrateful toward God and the Prophets, whom they ought to have regarded as fathers. See, besides those who have written expressly on Matthew and Luke, Isidore of Pelusium, Epistle 105, and the Interpretations of the Parables of the Gospel ascribed to Athanasius, Question 20. To me it does not seem likely that a fabulous matter is alluded to, or that God and the Prophets are in this way compared with vipers. I therefore side with those who understand here the very wicked sons of very wicked parents. That is, κακοῦ κόρακος κακὸν ὠὸν [kakou korakos kakon ōon], A bad crow lays a bad egg. With this in view the martyr Stephen addresses the Jews thus, Act. VII, 51. O stiff-necked, and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers were, so are you also. And long before, David, Psalm. LXXVIII, 8: That they might not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, etc. Nor shall I much object if someone understands by the name of vipers the demons; why these are signified by serpents is known to everyone. Moreover, all who rebel against God are reckoned sons of the devil. Accordingly Paul calls the magician Elymas a son of the devil, Act. XIII, 8. And Christ says to the Jews, Ioh. VIII, 44. You are of your father, the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. The δεινῆς ἐχίδνης θρέμμα [deinēs echidnēs thremma] in Sophocles' Trachiniae, line 1106, is something else. For there ἐχίδνη [echidnē] is not a viper but the fabulous Echidna, from whom Cerberus was born; for it is he who is spoken of there.
